nodes.title: Owner 2026-10-10: 'Don't go too Indian; be modern, futuristic, engaging and cool, the vibe Gen Alpha likes' (look and feel of the app, worlds and games)

Look-and-feel re-skin before Kaksha merges: global modern English UI names (no Meri Kaksha, Basti, Ganit/Vigyan/Bhasha), the Indian-town settlement becomes a futuristic base or colony, saffron accent replaced by a neon or electric sci-fi system, new English names for Antariksh and Khand, Gen-Alpha engagement patterns (skins, emotes, juicy feedback) with no coins, streaks, leaderboards or loot boxes; lesson language stays the child's

md.decisions: - `dc-r4-futurist-reskin` (2026-10-10): following owner-modern-futurist-vibe-20261010, Kaksha's look and feel is re-skinned before it merges. (1) User-facing names are modern English: the world and its base switch get new names (K proposes 3 each; no famous game names), the subject rings read Maths / Science / Language / EVS, and the brand stays Taxila. (2) The Nagar-style Indian town (bazaar rows, stepwell) becomes a futuristic base or colony on the planet (domes, labs, solar arrays, launch pad), keeping every rule: earned only by secured skills, deterministic placement, no counts. (3) The kesar/saffron accent is replaced by a neon or electric sci-fi token system: dark holographic for older classes, bright playful sci-fi (not warm 'Dawn') for classes 1-4, with all floors held (contrast, 14 px, 44 px targets, reduced motion). (4) Antariksh and Khand get English game names (G1 and G2 propose 3 each). (5) Engagement patterns Gen Alpha responds to (collectible skins, loadouts, emotes, juicy feedback and sound, a level-up moment in the Debrief), still with no coins, streaks, leaderboards or loot boxes. (6) Lesson language stays the child's (Hinglish, Hindi or English): pedagogy, not vibe. The avatar's style is revisited the same way when avatar work resumes. Reverse if: the owner prefers a direction K renders that keeps more Indian elements, or the five-second child test shows Indian children engage more with a local look.
